summary: Grok 4.6 is xAI's August 2026 successor to Grok 4.5, with a dedicated card emphasizing stronger agentic coding, knowledge-work, engineering, CAD, AI R&D, and inference-optimization capabilities. The safety material reports below-threshold dual-use biology capability and stronger refusal metrics in some areas, while also documenting regressions in factuality and several behavioral or mental-health measurements.

capabilities.text: The model accepts text and images and produces text, with listed availability through xAI's API, Grok Build, Cursor, Office add-ins, and gateways.
Training ran longer than Grok 4.5 and used curated synthetic trajectories, engineering data, improved optimization, and agentic reinforcement-learning environments.
Coding coverage spans IDE tasks, observability work, PR-quality rubrics, long-horizon repository work, and terminal workflows.
Knowledge-work capability is measured through GDPVal, AA-Briefcase, APEX-Agents, OfficeQA Pro, and a legal-agent benchmark.
Physical-engineering and CAD evaluations include EEBench, 3DCodeBench, PartBench, CADGenBench, and CADBench.
AI R&D capability includes an inference-optimization exercise plus MTS, InferenceEval, and KernelBenchInternal v1.1.
Search and factuality are covered by an internal hallucination benchmark and DeepSearchQA.

evaluations.context: Security fixes without new security regressions

safety_findings.text: The revision log says the final card corrects HackerBench v0.2, self-harm, MASK, and LAB figures.
HackerBench under release safeguards reports 6.9% harmful or dual-use compliance and 0.0% benign refusal for Grok 4.6.
The card places dual-use biology and chemistry capability below FAIF thresholds while reporting VCT 67.4%, Biosecurity VCT 47.8%, and BioUseBench severity-5 refusal 90.7%.
Jailbreak compliance is 0.04% for standard attacks, 3.9% for StrongReject, and 1.0% for long-horizon attacks.
General harmful-request compliance is 0.93%, child-safety compliance is 0.0%, and CBRN bio and chem refusal recall are both 100.0%.
Self-harm, MASK-Rectified, and sycophancy measurements are worse than the Grok 4.5 comparison values in the card.

limitations.text: The card requires human oversight and domain expertise for high-stakes medical, legal, financial, and safety-critical uses.
The documented modality is text output from text and image inputs, not a broader multimodal generation claim.
Pretraining cuts off in January 2026 even though supplemental data extends later.
The August revision corrected several results, so earlier numbers may be stale.
The hallucination rate is higher than the Grok 4.5 comparison number reported in the same chart.
Unrestricted cyber and biology evaluations measure capability rather than deployed policy behavior.

practical_implications.text: Use Grok 4.6 for long, tool-heavy coding tasks when the workflow can require tests, diffs, and human review.
Consider it for observability, repository triage, and engineering/CAD-adjacent work, but do not generalize every benchmark outside its harness.
Cite the revision date when discussing safety or benchmark numbers because the card records corrected results.
Keep security work authorized and sandboxed, with narrow tool permissions and no sensitive production context.
Demand source grounding for factual research because stronger agentic scores do not imply lower hallucination than Grok 4.5.

coverage_notes: This digest covers all 42 pages of the dedicated Grok 4.6 card. It includes the changelog because the card itself flags additions and corrected results in the final revision.
